output_json.patch_notes: Added a private static helper `resolveDestinationFile(File outputDir, String name)` in ZipUtil.java that builds the candidate destination File and then verifies, via canonical-path comparison, that it is equal to or nested under the canonical path of the given base directory; if not, it throws a ZipException identifying the offending entry name. This helper replaces every raw `new File(outputDir, name)` (and equivalent) sink that the finder's traces identified across the three vulnerable extraction branches: (1) `Unpacker.process` (used by all `unpack(...)` overloads and by `explode`), (2) `BackslashUnpacker.process` (both the per-segment directory-creation loop and the final file resolution, plus the top-level-file branch), and (3) `Unwraper.process` (used by all `unwrap(...)` overloads). For BackslashUnpacker, each intermediate path segment is validated against its immediate parent, which — since that parent was itself validated in the prior loop iteration (or is outputDir itself) — transitively guarantees every constructed path stays within outputDir, blocking traversal at any segment depth. Also added three regression tests to ZipUtilTest.java (testUnpackPreventsZipSlip, testUnwrapPreventsZipSlip, testUnpackBackslashesPreventsZipSlip) that build a ZIP with a traversal entry name (e.g. '../evil.txt', 'root/../../evil.txt', '..\\..\\evil.txt') and assert a ZipException is thrown and no file is written outside the target directory.
output_json.risk_notes: Legitimate use is unaffected: entries that resolve within outputDir (including the common case of an entry canonically equal to outputDir itself) are still permitted. Malicious/traversal entries now fail fast with a ZipException instead of silently writing outside the target directory (fail-closed behavior). One pre-existing, unrelated test failure (FilePermissionsTest.testPreserveWriteFlag) was observed both before and after this change when running under the provided Docker image (looks like a container/root-user file-permission artifact, unrelated to this patch) — full `mvn test` output was diffed against the unpatched baseline to confirm it is not a regression. All 48 ZipUtilTest cases (45 original + 3 new) and the rest of the suite (119 total tests, only the pre-existing unrelated failure) pass.
output_json.summary: Fixed a Zip Slip / path traversal vulnerability (CWE-22) in org.zeroturnaround.zip.ZipUtil where ZIP entry names were concatenated with the extraction target directory without verifying the resulting path stayed within that directory, allowing a crafted ZIP entry (e.g. containing '../' or backslash-encoded traversal sequences) to write files anywhere on the filesystem reachable by the process.
